question: A provision appears under a Guidance heading and uses the word 'should.' Is it mandatory, and when may a deviation be appropriate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No, a Guidance provision is not mandatory. By definition, Guidance is a statement of recommended practice in typical situations, and deviations are allowed when engineering judgment or an engineering study indicates the deviation to be appropriate. Only Standard provisions (using "shall") are mandatory. Standards (mandatory): - "Guidance-a statement of recommended practice in typical situations, with deviations allowed if engineering judgment or engineering study (see Section 1D.03) indicates the deviation to be appropriate. All Guidance statements are labeled, and the text appears in unbold italic type. The verb 'should' is typically used. The verbs 'shall' and 'may' are not used in Guidance statements. Guidance statements are sometimes modified by Option statements." - By contrast, "Standard-a statement of required, mandatory, or specifically prohibitive practice regarding a traffic control device," in which "The verb 'shall' is typically used." Citations: - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) Note: Section 1D.03 (Support) explains that the application of engineering study and engineering judgment is a fundamental principle of the use of traffic control devices, which is the mechanism by which deviations from Guidance (and, in limited documented cases, even from Standards) are determined to be appropriate. - Section 1D.03 Support §2 (p.32)
gold_answer: It is recommended practice, not a mandatory Standard. A deviation may be appropriate when engineering judgment or an engineering study indicates that the deviation is suitable for the specific situation.
